# Hermes Agent: Complete Onboarding & Troubleshooting FAQ

### 1. Installation, Platform Support & Updates
- **Windows (Native vs. WSL2)**: Windows 10/11 is Tier 1 supported via the PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`) without WSL. WSL2 is only recommended if you use the web dashboard embedded terminal chat (`/chat`), which requires a POSIX PTY.
- **Docker & NAS Deployments**: Docker images (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`) support multi-arch (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` for Raspberry Pi/Apple Silicon). On NAS devices (UGOS Pro, Synology, unRAID) with volume permission issues, pass `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) environment variables (e.g., `PUID=1000 PGID=10`).
- **Android / Termux**: Supported natively via `install.sh`. It automatically detects Termux, sets `$TMPDIR` paths, and installs the curated `[termux-all]` dependency group (also updated via `hermes update`).
- **Web Dashboard**: Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local web UI and browser chat at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`.
- **Update Latency**: If `hermes update` appears stuck during Node.js dependency updates, Camofox is downloading browser binaries in the background without terminal output.

---

### 2. Model Providers & API Configuration
- **Small Local Models (Ollama/Qwen 4B–9B)**: Slow response times occur because Hermes sends the full ~45-tool schema on every turn. Optimize by disabling unneeded tools (`hermes tools`), using faster quantizations or 32B+ models, and setting `terminal.backend: local`.
- **Local Endpoint Overrides (`provider: custom`)**: If Hermes routes to external APIs despite local `base_url`, change `provider: auto` to `provider: custom` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to prevent auto-detecting ambient environment keys (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).
- **Claude Pro/Max vs. API Billing**: Anthropic bills all API keys as per-token API usage. To consume Claude Pro/Max subscription allowances in Hermes, authenticate via Claude OAuth instead of API keys.
- **Azure AI Foundry & Ollama Cloud**:
  - *Azure AI Foundry*: Run `hermes setup` or set `provider: azure-foundry` and `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`. (Claude Code-specific env vars like `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` are ignored).
  - *Ollama Cloud*: Use provider `ollama-cloud` (routes to OpenAI-compatible `https://ollama.com/v1`, avoiding 404s at `/api`).
- **Google Gemini**: Legacy `google-gemini-cli` OAuth was removed. Use Google AI Studio with `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` or Vertex AI.
- **Local Honcho Memory**: Point `base_url` to your local instance (e.g., `http://localhost:8000`); Hermes automatically injects `"local"` placeholder credentials to avoid SDK validation errors.
- **Vision Models & Token Tracking**: Add `supports_vision: true` to custom/Ollama model configs for native image payloads. Streaming OpenAI-compatible endpoints automatically receive `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` for `/usage` tracking.
- **Model Routing Policy**: Complexity-based automatic model routing (`smart_model_routing`) is not supported. Use manual switching (`/model` or `hermes chat -m <model>`) or subagent delegation (`delegation.model`).

---

### 3. Messaging Gateways, Media & Personas
- **Interactive Gateway Setup**: Run `hermes gateway setup` to configure Discord, Telegram, and other messaging platforms via an interactive CLI wizard.
- **Telegram User Authorization**: `allowed_chats` is only a group-chat filter, not for direct messages. To authorize a DM user, add your numeric user ID under `telegram.allow_from` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, approve a pairing code with `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`, or set `telegram.allow_all: true`.
- **Files & Media Handling**:
  - *Inbound*: Small code/text files (`.py`, `.txt`) uploaded to Discord/Telegram are injected directly into context; other files are cached.
  - *Outbound*: Agents deliver generated files via Matrix `m.file`, Email attachments, DingTalk Markdown (`![image](url)`), and Telegram media. Tool results with `MEDIA:<path>` tags are forwarded automatically.
- **Personas & Profiles**: Set per-channel system prompts via `channel_prompts` in platform configs. For multiple accounts (e.g., WeChat/Weixin), run multiplexed profile gateways to isolate credentials, sessions, and memory.
- **Session Restores**: Crashed or interrupted gateway sessions enter `resume_pending` state instead of wiping transcripts; resume anytime using `/resume`. `session_reset` defaults to `none`.

---

### 4. Agent Loops, Memory, Tools & Observability
- **Tool Call Limits & Autonomy**: Default turn limit is `agent.max_turns: 90` (override per session via `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). On limit exhaustion, Hermes finalizes cleanly. For long autonomous workflows, use `/goal <task>` (Ralph loop), which persists across sessions and resumes with `/goal resume`.
- **Subagents**: Use the `delegate_task` tool to spawn isolated child `AIAgent` instances (supports parallel batch execution).
- **Core Memory Files & Context**:
  - `SOUL.md`: System persona, character, and instructions.
  - `USER.md`: User profile, identity, and personal preferences (`target="user"`).
  - `MEMORY.md`: Long-term global knowledge and stored facts.
  - `ContextCompressor`: Automatically prunes older verbose tool outputs; pluggable engines configured via `context.engine`.
- **Custom Tools & Memory Plugins**: In-tree `plugins/memory/` additions are closed. Install standalone memory plugins implementing `MemoryProvider` into `~/.hermes/plugins/`. Add personal tools via plugins and enable with `hermes plugins enable <name>`.
- **Diagnostics, Telemetry & Tracing**:
  - Run `hermes doctor` to verify environment, auth, and configuration health.
  - Track skill usage with `/insights` or `hermes insights` (backed by `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`).
  - Trace tool call chains and nested inputs/outputs with Langfuse via `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Security Vulnerabilities**: Report security issues privately via GitHub Security Advisories or by emailing `security@nousresearch.com`. Do not file public issues.
